A quick technical summary from the bridge (details below). TL;DR: autoscaler + routing config overlap caused KV-cache invalidation and a short period of sustained GC/queueing on the serving hosts which led to timeouts and elevated error rates.

Timeline (UTC):
- 15:42 UTC — rolling config update initiated for canary pools (internal autoscaler tuning).
- 15:44 UTC — several GPU workers restarted as part of the rollout; cache warm-up sequence triggered.
- 15:45–15:58 UTC — observed KV cache thrash: cache misses rose from ~3% to ~68% on affected hosts; CPU and host-side queue latency increased.
- 15:47–15:55 UTC — the routing layer attempted to fall back to a cheaper variant; a mis-evaluated health check caused additional re-routes and some 4xx/5xx responses.

Immediate mitigations performed:
1) Paused the autoscaler rollout and pinned the canary pool versions.
2) Forced graceful restart of affected GPU instances to clear unhealthy state and ensured KV cache warmup via background prefetch.
3) Adjusted routing health-check window to avoid flapping during restarts.

Next steps (proposed):
- Hotfix: increase health-check stabilization window + decouple routing fallback logic from autoscaler rollouts (owner: jonas_weber) — target: 2028-08-21T16:00:00-07:00
- Config change: autoscaler backoff tuning to prevent parallel restarts (owner: karthik_iyer) — target: 2028-08-23T23:59:00-07:00
- Post-incident capacity test and controlled rollout plan for model variants (owner: kimberly_park) — target: 2028-08-30

I've attached a short timeline log and a link to the Jira ticket HZ-1234 with trace snippets.

Jonas

Hi Maya / Tom — attached is the formal RCA (ACME_RCA_v1.pdf) and the action tracker (acme-followup-action-tracker.xlsx). Summary below: 

Root cause (short): An overlap between an autoscaler configuration rollout and routing fallback logic caused a cascade: worker restarts triggered KV-cache invalidation and heavy cache-miss penalties, which pushed request latency up and led the routing layer to perform aggressive fallbacks; an edge health-check flapping condition then returned a subset of 4xx/5xx responses.

Impact: ~25 minutes of elevated p95 latency (peak p95 1.8s vs baseline 320ms), throughput reduction ~38%, and a small number of client-facing 5xx errors affecting checkout traffic across us-west and us-east. No data loss.

Committed corrective actions (owners & due dates):
- HZ-1234: Hotfix to decouple fallback from autoscaler rollouts — owner: jonas_weber — due: 2028-08-21
- HZ-1235: Autoscaler backoff tuning and safer rollout window — owner: karthik_iyer — due: 2028-08-23
- HZ-1236: Controlled canary rollout playbook & capacity test — owner: kimberly_park — due: 2028-08-30
- Weekly progress summary to ACME execs for 6 weeks — owner: avery_johnson — start: 2028-08-24

Please see the tracker for status, owners, and verification criteria. We'll share a short executive one-pager for your leadership team by Monday.

Attachments: ACME_RCA_v1.pdf (formal RCA, includes timeline and trace snippets), acme-followup-action-tracker.xlsx (live tracker with owners/dates/verification).

If you prefer a short sync, I can set up a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to walk through the RCA and acceptance criteria.

Thanks again for your partnership; we'll own the delivery until all items are closed.

Best,
